debrief.whyItWorks: With limited clock, taking space while the defence is unsettled is the most reliable way to plant in time. Here, 2 players faced 2 with about 35 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It spends the team's options at once, leaving little for the post-plant.
debrief.assumption: The defenders cannot rotate enough players to the site before the plant.
debrief.breaksWhen: The defence stacks the chosen site and has its own utility ready for the execute.

evidenceReview.explanation: The team had one molotov and no smokes, flashes or HE grenades. The utility left sets how much of the plan can be forced rather than hoped for.
The round clock stood near 35 seconds. The round clock bounds how long any plan can take.
It was 2 players against 2. The head count sets how many duels the team can lose and still carry out its plan.
Two defenders could not be placed. Unaccounted-for opponents are the main risk to any committed plan and the main reason to gather information.
The team's players stood as follows: two in Middle. Where the team starts sets how quickly it can act together.

debrief.followupReview: The proposed best answer to the new information was: Change your line to use the new information. Reasoning: the new information shows where an opponent is or what utility they have used, so adapting the plan is worth more than repeating it.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to gather information before acting, spending clock to reduce the guess.

counterfactual.changedFact: The defenders are known to be stacked on the site you would hit.
counterfactual.effect: The execute meets a full defence, and taking information or faking becomes stronger.
